title.narrative: Multipurpose Cash Assistance for IDP and Famine Response, Sudan

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed project 'Multipurpose Cash Assistance for IDP and Famine Response, Sudan’ will target 2,350 vulnerable households (HHs) of internally displaced persons (IDPs) in Heiban county. 2,350 HHs are estimated to include 11,750 direct unique individuals (6,345F 5,405 M). The project will provide multipurpose cash assistance (MPCA) by using the Cash over counter by pre-contracted financial service providers (FSP) to allow conflict-affected (IDPs and vulnerable host community members) to address their basic needs, using a harmonised approach in coordination with other aid agencies. It will do so through one (1) distribution of 100 USD to each targeted HH, representing an estimated 70% of the revised minimum expenditure basket (MEB) for Sudan suggested and adopted by Cash Working Group in August 2024. The target HHs have already been registered but are yet to receive assistance due to blockage of doing MPCA through LEM, a South Sudan based financial service provider. NRC is considering the option of using mountain trade and development bank (MTDB) for cash distribution, which is a local based financial institution with limited capacity to pre-finance cash distribution. To address this, NRC proposes to engage LEM for cash drop in Kauda and MTDB for cash distribution in the field on a pilot basis. This appears to be one of the options in favour of the authority's position on the use of FSP and could hopefully unblock the challenge around the use of FSP. NRC has invited MTDB to express interest in the tender process for engagement as FSP and the application is currently under consideration. ltbrgt ltbrgtNRC initially planned to intervene in Habila and Heiban counties, using complementary donor funding for blanket MPCA in target camps. However, delays due to Financial Service Provider restrictions led to reallocating donor funding elsewhere. As households in Heiban were already identified and registered, this revision aims to support them, increasing project coverage from 1,609 to 2,350 households. This ensures better support for IDP camps and host communities, prevents negative coping mechanisms, and allows rapid implementation as registration is complete. ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe proposed project will contribute to the Strategic Objective 3 from the 2024 Sudan Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan, which is to ‘Provide safe, equitable, dignified and unhindered access to critical basic services and livelihoods opportunities for the most vulnerable groups to prevent further erosion of their coping abilities’, as well as contribute to one of two Cash Working Group objectives: ‘Most vulnerable individuals near markets, but without access to general food assistance, receive repeated multipurpose cash (MPC) and are able to prioritize a variety of basic needs, reducing reliance on negative coping strategies over time’. ltbrgt ltbrgtThrough proactive engagement with community-based structures and local actors, the project will support the localization agenda and strategy. It will complement NRC's ongoing MPCA response and leverage the expertise of NRC's Emergency Response and Livelihoods and Food Security teams. Adopting Safe and Inclusive Programming, the project will ensure the mainstreaming of protection, conflict sensitivity, and Do No Harm principles, with 15% of the participants expected to be Persons with Disability (PwD), or approximately 1,763 individuals (952F 811M). To manage risks, the project will employ an adaptive management approach informed by regular monitoring of the context and protection environment. NRC's expertise in MPCA and presence in South Kordofan make it well-suited for this project. Coordination with other actors ensures a harmonized cash approach, with post-distribution monitoring (PDM) to assess impact and improve efforts. NRC also works closely with humanitarian actors to mitigate unintended ripple effects, aligning aid types and schedules across South Kordofan, including targeted project areas.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgt
